_schema.description: Severstal steel defect segmentation - shared results across all approaches.
_schema.metric: Dice, computed by evaluate.py / evaluate_head.py with GLOBAL (dataset-level) intersection and sum accumulation, not per-image averaging.
_schema.split: All headline numbers are on the held-out TEST split (1886 images) unless stated. Hyperparameter selection was done on VAL only.
_schema.mean_dice_1_4: Mean Dice over defect classes 1-4, excluding background. This is the headline comparison number.
_schema.backbone: facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m, FROZEN in every run below (no backbone gradients).

dataset.split_method: stratified 70/15/15 by class-presence combination, grouped by ImageId
dataset.pixel_overlap_between_classes: none (verified empirically across all 427 multi-class images)

A1a_linear_lightlytrain.description: LightlyTrain dinov3/vits16-linear. Frozen backbone + single linear layer. Unweighted CrossEntropy (hardcoded in library), full untouched background distribution.
A1a_linear_lightlytrain.note: Total collapse on classes 1 and 2 - unweighted CE at ~2% positive rate learns to never predict rare classes.

A1b_eomt.description: LightlyTrain dinov3/vits16-eomt. Frozen backbone + EoMT (Mask2Former-style) decoder with Hungarian matching and mask+dice+class loss.
A1b_eomt.note: Stronger decoder + Dice loss term improved common classes; rare classes still ~zero.

A1c_eomt_oversampled.description: As A1b, trained on hardlink-oversampled train set (class 2 x10, classes 1/4 x3) = 12678 images.
A1c_eomt_oversampled.note: First non-zero class-2 result. Confirmed exposure/imbalance was implicated.

A1d_eomt_oversampled_31ep.description: As A1c, trained to LightlyTrain's documented EoMT convergence benchmark (~31 epochs).
A1d_eomt_oversampled_31ep.note: Best EoMT result. Checkpoint selected by aggregate mIoU, which traded class 2 away for gains elsewhere.

prototype_cosine_trainingfree.description: Training-free: mean class-2 and background prototype vectors from frozen features, nearest-prototype with a threshold calibrated on train.
prototype_cosine_trainingfree.note: Class 2 only. Calibration-set Dice 0.54 vs test 0.009 - the difference-of-means direction is not the discriminative direction, so this understates what the features support.

B1_linear_head_cached.description: Frozen DINOv3 at NATIVE 256x1600 resolution (16x100 patch grid), features cached once, linear head trained with class-weight exponent selected on val.

B2_mlp_head_cached.description: As B1 but with an MLP head: Linear(384->256) + GELU + Linear(256->5).
B2_mlp_head_cached.note: Beats the 9.2-hour EoMT run on classes 1, 2 and 4; essentially ties on class 3.

B3_mlp_head_multilayer.description: As B2 but features are blocks (2,5,8,11) concatenated instead of the final layer only. Each block is LayerNorm'd before concatenation - raw ViT activations grow ~59x in magnitude from block 2 to block 11, so without this the deepest layer dominates and early edge/texture layers are ignored.
B3_mlp_head_multilayer.note: Beats the 9.2-hour EoMT run on ALL FOUR defect classes. Reaches 70% of the stride-16 patch-grid oracle ceiling.

B4_conv_subpatch_dice.description: Conv head (3x3 spatial context) over cached full spatial multi-layer DINOv3 maps, with PixelShuffle x4 sub-patch output (stride 4) and weighted CE + soft-Dice loss. Backbone still the same FROZEN dinov3-vits16.
B4_conv_subpatch_dice.note: Superseded by B5/B6 below. Test mean Dice 0.6605 vs 0.5297 for B3 and 0.3107 for the 9.2-hour EoMT run. Class 2 went 0.0018 (A1d) -> 0.5536. 71% of the stride-4 oracle ceiling (0.936). weight_power=0.30 here was calibrated at output stride 16 (before PixelShuffle was added) and reused unchanged - see A3 below for what happened when this was corrected.

A3_convnext_vs_vit_recalibration.description: spec A3 (ViT vs ConvNeXt ablation) plus a fairness check: B4's weight_power was tuned at stride 16, before PixelShuffle x4 was added, and never re-tuned for the stride-4 label distribution (bg:c2 goes from 2631:1 at stride 16 to ~10413:1 at stride 4). Recalibrated (wp=0.50) and ran DINOv3-ConvNeXt-Tiny FPN head side by side, matched as closely as possible: same output stride (4), same weight_power (0.50), comparable head size (925,893 vs 1,004,112 params).
A3_convnext_vs_vit_recalibration.convnext_backbone: facebook/dinov3-convnext-tiny-pretrain-lvd1689m, 27.8M params, frozen. No feature cache - multi-scale maps at stride 4 would need ~648GB; backbone runs on the fly instead (14.6ms/img, faster than ViT-S's 24.8ms/img since there is no quadratic attention).
A3_convnext_vs_vit_recalibration.convnext_head: Per-stage GroupNorm(1,C) [equalises stage scales - raw ConvNeXt activations differ ~11x in mean magnitude between stage 2 and stage 3, same trap as the ViT multi-layer experiment] -> 1x1 project to 128ch -> bilinear align to stride 4 -> concat -> two 3x3 convs -> 1x1 output.
A3_convnext_vs_vit_recalibration.verdict: ViT-S + PixelShuffle beats ConvNeXt-T FPN on every single class at a fair, matched comparison, despite ConvNeXt having genuinely native stride-4 features and 29% more backbone parameters. This was NOT the expected outcome - the patch-grid oracle analysis correctly identified resolution as the dominant lever, but native fine-grained features did not translate into better results, most plausibly because ConvNeXt-T's frozen features are less informative for this domain than ViT-S's (untested directly - no per-class AUC probe was run for ConvNeXt).
A3_convnext_vs_vit_recalibration.important_methodological_note: Recalibrating B4's weight_power improved VAL (0.6721 -> 0.6731, a real but tiny gain) but made TEST WORSE (0.6605 -> 0.6304). The original wp=0.30 checkpoint remains the best validated result and was NOT replaced. This is the second time in this project that a val improvement under ~0.01 failed to hold on test - at these margins val differences are closer to noise than signal, and test should be checked sparingly, not after every micro-tuning step.

spatial_head_ablation.description: Incremental ablation over cached FULL SPATIAL DINOv3 feature maps (multi-layer blocks 2/5/8/11, per-layer LayerNorm'd). Each step changes exactly ONE thing. All numbers are PIXEL-LEVEL Dice on val, predictions upsampled to 256x1600, so they are comparable to each other and to A1a-B3.
spatial_head_ablation.weight_power_note: Calibrated empirically on this cache. The spatial cache keeps ALL 1600 patches/image so bg:c2 is 2631:1, vs 282:1 in the old flat cache which had subsampled background. The flat cache's -0.5 is badly wrong here and collapsed c2 to 0.0000. Measured curve: -0.15:0.314 -0.05:0.337 0.05:0.371 0.15:0.454 0.30:0.535 0.45:0.481 0.60:0.413 0.75:0.343 0.90:0.282 (subset-trained, patch-grid metric, used for ranking only).

A1_plus_depth.isolates: extra layer, 1x1 kernel - NO spatial mixing (null control)

B_plus_subpatch.isolates: PixelShuffle x4 - OUTPUT RESOLUTION (largest single gain)

C_plus_dice.isolates: soft-Dice loss term added to weighted CE

findings: Depth alone contributes nothing (-0.0014). The control worked: it means A2's gain is attributable to the 3x3 kernel, not to added layers or parameters.
Output resolution was the single largest lever (+0.075), confirming the patch-grid oracle analysis that identified quantisation as the binding constraint for thin defects.

METHODOLOGICAL: train_spatial.py's in-loop metric scores on the PATCH GRID, which hides upsampling error and is not comparable across output strides - under it, increment B (the biggest real win) looked like a regression. All reported numbers use evaluate_spatial.py, which upsamples to pixel level. Epoch selection still used the patch-grid metric, so saved checkpoints are the best patch-level epoch, not necessarily the best pixel-level one.

B5_frozen_wide_head_long.description: As B4 but head width 256 -> 1024 and 30 epochs instead of 12. Backbone still frozen.

B6_lora_adapted.description: BEST RESULT. Same head as B5, plus LoRA (r=16, alpha=32) on q/k/v of all 12 DINOv3 blocks - 442,368 trainable backbone params, 2.0% of the backbone. Head initialised from the B5 checkpoint (LP-FT: fine-tuning from a trained probe avoids random-head gradients distorting pretrained weights). Trained at native 256x1600 (measured 1.11 GB peak at batch 4 - SDPA never materialises the 1600x1600 attention matrix), 8 epochs.
B6_lora_adapted.why_lora_not_partial_unfreeze: The head taps blocks 2/5/8/11. Unfreezing only the last N blocks would leave the early taps frozen while late ones adapt. LoRA moves all taps together.
B6_lora_adapted.note: Best val was at the LAST epoch (8), so the run had not converged - more epochs may help, though the frozen 12->30 epoch experiment suggests the gain would be small. Rank 16 is untested against the r=3-9 suggested by the DINOv3 fine-tuning repo.

bottleneck_diagnosis.description: Three levers tested against the ~0.24 gap between our result and the stride-4 oracle ceiling (0.936), to determine whether the head, the training budget, or the frozen features were the binding constraint.

train_vs_test_gap.note: B4 checkpoint evaluated on the TRAIN split. Train 0.7016 / val 0.6920 / test 0.6605 - a train-val gap of only 0.010. This is UNDERFITTING, not overfitting: the model barely fits data it has seen better than data it has not.
train_vs_test_gap.correction: This refuted the 'class 2 fails because only 173 training images' explanation asserted earlier in the project. Scarcity predicts memorisation plus a large train-test gap. Measured instead: c2 underfit gap (ceiling 0.905 -> train 0.615) = 0.29, generalisation gap (train 0.615 -> test 0.554) = 0.06. Underfitting dominates ~5:1.

head_capacity_scan.note: conv head width scaled with everything else held fixed. Cell-level val.
head_capacity_scan.conclusion: Each ~3x in parameters buys roughly half the previous gain (+0.0136 then +0.0061). Plateaus near 0.71; no plausible head size closes a 0.22 gap.

epoch_scan.note: hidden=1024, 12 vs 30 epochs, cosine stretched over the full run.
epoch_scan.conclusion: +0.0018 for 2.5x the training, while train loss more than halved (0.188 -> 0.089) and val DECLINED after epoch 16. Not optimisation-limited.

lora_adaptation.note: The direct test of whether the frozen features were the constraint. Pixel-level, matched evaluation.
lora_adaptation.conclusion: Real and consistent across both splits, but modest - the same order as head capacity scaling. Adapting the features was NOT a dramatic unlock.

lora_rank_sweep.note: alpha scaled as 2r so the effective update scale (alpha/r) is held constant and rank is isolated. 8 epochs each, everything else identical. Best val, pixel-level.
lora_rank_sweep.conclusion: SUPERSEDED - this conclusion was wrong. Original reading: 'adapter capacity is not the constraint; r=32 was not run because a flat response across 4x makes it near-certainly flat too.' Full fine-tuning (B7) then beat r=16 by +0.011 val. The flat response was real but the inference from it was not: r=4/8/16 is only 1%-4% of ViT-S's d=384, and all three runs shared the same restriction to q/k/v with the MLP blocks never adapted at all. A flat response inside a narrow band, under a fixed module restriction, says nothing about the ceiling outside it.
lora_rank_sweep.what_would_have_caught_it: Varying module coverage as well as rank. Rank and target-module set are two independent axes; only one was swept, and the conclusion was stated over both.

bottleneck_diagnosis.overall_conclusion: Revised after the augmented 1e-4 run. Cumulative val has moved 0.6932 -> 0.7325 (+0.039) since the point at which this project concluded that every lever was flat and the residual gap was probably label noise. That conclusion was wrong, and wrong for three separate reasons: the flat LoRA rank sweep was confined to 1%-4% of full rank with MLP blocks never adapted; augmentation was ruled out under an underfitting diagnosis that expired once full FT overfit; and LR was swept without augmentation, which understated its value by 3x. Class 2, the axis that looked most stubbornly flat, moved from 0.61-0.64 to 0.6646 once LR and augmentation were combined. The remaining gap to the 0.936 stride-4 oracle is still 0.20 and label noise is still a plausible contributor, but it has not been tested and nothing currently measured supports it. The best model is not converged.
methodological_corrections: Attributed a 0.7135-vs-0.6929 discrepancy to bf16 precision. WRONG - fp32 re-evaluation gave 0.7028 vs bf16's 0.7030, i.e. precision costs nothing. The real cause was cell-level vs pixel-level metric, a distinction already identified earlier in the project and then forgotten when making the comparison.

Called the first three LoRA epochs a monotonic decline and 'genuine overfitting rather than noise', and was one epoch from killing the run. Epoch 4 jumped to a new best and it finished as the best model of the project.

Initially planned partial unfreezing of the last 4 blocks. This would have left blocks 2 and 5 - two of the four layers the head taps - frozen while blocks 8 and 11 adapted. LoRA on all 12 blocks avoids that inconsistency.

Concluded 'adapter capacity is not the constraint' from a rank sweep that held the target-module set fixed at q/k/v. Rank and module coverage are independent axes; sweeping one and concluding over both was the error. Full fine-tuning refuted it by +0.011. Stating a conclusion over a wider space than the sweep actually covered is the general failure mode.

Deferred augmentation on the grounds that the model was underfitting. That was correct at the time but became stale the moment full FT crossed into overfitting; the re-check was prompted by noticing the regime change, not scheduled. Diagnoses that gate future work need re-testing when the thing they were conditioned on changes.

Swept LR and augmentation as independent axes and extrapolated the LR curve's flattening across the augmented setting. They interact; the extrapolation understated the combined gain by 3x. Flattening measured under one condition does not transfer to another condition that changes the overfitting regime.

Projected B9's test score at 0.7235 and budgeted only ~0.003 for selection pressure. Actual was 0.7104, a gap of +0.0221 versus the +0.0060 historical mean. Selection was applied twice over the same val split - across configs AND across epochs within the winner - and the compounding was underestimated. The tell was visible beforehand: the rare classes c1/c2 are exactly where val estimates are noisiest, and they are exactly where the test drop concentrated.

Reported per-class Dice at each config's val-chosen min_area while the adjacent column was labelled unfiltered - two filter settings in one table row. Caught only because the min_area filter was questioned on principle; the numbers were 0.015 low on c1/c2 for the configs that chose a large threshold.

Concluded from val that augmentation and high LR stack superadditively (+0.0151). On test the same comparison is -0.0075. Every config in the ladder had been ranked on a val split that had already been used for both config selection and epoch selection; only a held-out measurement exposed it.

The 32-epoch run's saved checkpoint scores 0.7283 on val but sits 4.6 sigma above its own local neighbourhood and 12.5 sigma above its settled tail. Reporting best-epoch-on-val as the run's result would have overstated it by ~0.006. Best-of-N-epochs selection is not free, and N=32 makes it worse than N=12.

Ran the entire config search before ever measuring run-to-run variance. The test sd is 0.0017 and the val sd 0.0043, so a large fraction of the rankings compared in this project - and nearly every per-class claim about c1/c2 - were inside the noise band. Measuring the noise floor first would have avoided several hours of runs and at least four unsupported conclusions.

Declared augmentation harmful at 4.7 sigma based on a test split drawn from the training distribution. On Kaggle's hidden set the sign flips: +0.0149 private. The statistics were sound; the split could not measure the quantity augmentation improves. Held-out data from the SAME distribution does not validate robustness interventions.

Extending a well-regularised run improved local test to the project's best value (0.7340) while degrading the target-distribution proxy. Under distribution shift, 'train until in-distribution metrics stop improving' is the wrong stopping rule - it trains away the regularisation that generalises.

Masked pretraining showed a healthy training curve (loss down 2.7x, cosine similarity up) while degrading the representation by 0.0655 on a matched frozen probe. A self-supervised objective improving does not mean the features improved - only a downstream probe answers that, and it must be gated BEFORE the expensive fine-tune, not after.

full_finetune.note: The decisive capacity test - full rank, every module. Best val, pixel-level fp32.
full_finetune.conclusion: Feature adaptation was NOT saturated. Full FT gave +0.011 over the best LoRA and +0.0005 over the best frozen head, and is the first configuration in the project to show real overfitting. LR mattered more than expected: 1e-5 landed at 0.7021, essentially identical to LoRA, and was still improving at epoch 11 - it is a slower traversal of the same path, not a different outcome. Since 5e-5 > 1e-5 the trend has not turned over, so the LR peak is still unlocated.

augmentation.note: Run only AFTER full FT pushed the model into overfitting. Best val, pixel-level fp32.
augmentation.conclusion: +0.0079, the second-largest single lever measured in this project after head capacity (+0.020), and larger than the entire 10x LR sweep (+0.0034 from 5e-5 to 1e-4). Confirms the regime diagnosis: while the model underfit, augmentation would have hurt; once full FT made it overfit, augmentation became the highest-value remaining lever.
augmentation.interaction_with_lr: LR and augmentation interact: the 5e-5->1e-4 step is worth +0.0034 unaugmented and +0.0106 augmented. Sweeping them independently and adding the results would have understated the combination by ~3x.

patch_grid_oracle.description: Upper bound on Dice for ANY per-patch classifier, computed by collapsing ground-truth masks to the patch grid and upsampling back. No model involved. Measures loss due purely to patch quantisation.

fpn_se_resnext50_kaggle.metric: Kaggle competition Dice (own aggregation, not directly comparable)

dinov3_convnext_mask2former.source: Gharbage et al., 'Rethinking Transfer Learning for Industrial Inspection' (arXiv 2605.23472)
dinov3_convnext_mask2former.metric: mIoU on their own Severstal split (Train 5332 / Val 1334 - excludes background-only images)
dinov3_convnext_mask2former.comparability_caveat: Their split has ~6666 images (defect-containing only); ours includes 5902 background-only images. Not a like-for-like comparison.

key_findings: Frozen DINOv3 features ARE strongly separable for every defect class. Held-out-IMAGE linear-probe AUC at native resolution: c1 0.912, c2 0.975, c3 0.877, c4 0.969. Class 2 - the one that kept failing - is the MOST separable.

Class 2's repeated failure was never a feature-quality or data-quantity problem. 173 training images suffice. It was caused by unweighted cross-entropy over an untouched ~2871:1 background:class-2 patch ratio.

Rebalancing via data sampling (keeping all defect patches, subsampling background ~10x at cache time) was more effective than loss reweighting. Stacking additional loss weights on top of that over-corrected and monotonically degraded results.
The class-weight exponent has a genuine interior optimum (-0.1 linear, -0.2 MLP); classes disagree about the ideal operating point, so the optimum is a compromise.
A ~100k-param MLP on cached frozen features outperforms a ~15M-param EoMT decoder trained for 9.2 hours, at a fraction of the compute.

Multi-layer features (blocks 2/5/8/11) gave +0.06 mean Dice over final-layer-only, and disproportionately helped the thin/rare classes: fraction-of-ceiling for c1 rose 47%->63% and c2 50%->64%, vs c4 78%->80%. This supports the hypothesis that early ViT blocks retain edge/texture detail the final block abstracts away.

METHODOLOGICAL: the HuggingFace AutoImageProcessor default resizes to 224x224 square, silently squashing 256x1600 images ~7x horizontally. This invalidated several early diagnostics until it was found and fixed in dino_features.py.

METHODOLOGICAL: concatenating raw multi-layer ViT features is a trap - block 11 activations are ~59x larger than block 2, so the deepest layer dominates. Per-layer LayerNorm before concatenation is required for multi-layer features to help at all.

Remaining headroom is now split between classification quality (0.530 of a 0.754 ceiling at the current grid) and output resolution (the 0.754 cap itself, liftable to 0.864 at 8px stride WITHOUT changing the backbone, via 2x-upsampled input or overlapping shifted inference).
not_yet_done: Approach B of the original spec: YOLOv8-seg (B1 plain, B2 DINOv3-distilled) - the project's core comparison arm
Finer output resolution (2x-upsampled input or overlapping shifted inference) - the largest remaining structural lever, raises the oracle cap from 0.754 to 0.864
Attention rollout and prediction-overlay figures (spec Stage 5)
Kaggle inference-kernel packaging for a private-leaderboard number
B9 is not converged - val never turned over in 16 epochs. A longer schedule (24-32 ep) has headroom.
Top-LR 2e-4 with augmentation is now worth testing: the 'LR is flattening' argument was measured unaugmented and does not hold here.

Only epoch 10 of B9 was ever evaluated on test; no other epoch was saved, so 'is epoch 10 a lucky epoch on val' cannot be checked without re-running - and checking it on test would itself be selecting on test.

B7_full_finetune.description: Full fine-tune of all 21,596,544 DINOv3 params (100% of backbone) + the same h1024 conv head, 12 epochs. Run to test whether the flat LoRA rank sweep really meant saturated adaptation. It did not.
B7_full_finetune.why_this_run_existed: The rank sweep was read as saturation, but that reading had two holes: (1) ViT-S has d=384, so r=4/8/16 spans only 1%-4% of full rank - a flat response inside a narrow low-rank band is not evidence of a ceiling; (2) LoRA targeted q_proj/k_proj/v_proj ONLY, never the MLP blocks, which hold ~2/3 of each block's parameters. Full FT removes both limits at once.

config.head_init: LP-FT from the B5 frozen checkpoint, same as B6

B7_full_finetune.why_gamma_085_not_075: 0.75 is the value usually quoted for ViT-S/16 classification, but our head taps blocks 2/5/8/11 and consumes early features directly. At 0.75, block 2 receives 0.75^10 = 5.6% of base LR and stays effectively frozen - silently re-imposing the very constraint this run existed to remove. 0.85 gives block 2 ~20%.

lr_sweep_val_pixel_fp32.peak_note: Monotone increasing across a 10x range (1e-5 -> 5e-5 -> 1e-4 = 0.7021 -> 0.7140 -> 0.7174), so the peak was never bracketed. But the gain is flattening hard: 1e-5->5e-5 bought +0.0120, 5e-5->1e-4 only +0.0034. The 1e-4 run was WORSE than 5e-5 through epochs 1-5 (dipping to 0.6735 at epoch 5) before overtaking from epoch 7 - the same dip-then-recover shape as the LoRA runs at epoch 3. Stopping early on that dip would have wrongly rejected the best LR.

B7_full_finetune.test: NOT YET EVALUATED - deliberately withheld while the LR peak is still unresolved (5e-5 > 1e-5 means the trend has not turned over)
B7_full_finetune.vs_lora_epoch_matched: Full FT ran 12 epochs vs LoRA's 8, so totals are unmatched. Matching at epoch 8 from the logs (both bf16): full FT 0.7130 vs LoRA 0.7030. The +0.010 is capacity, not schedule.

per_class_val_vs_lora.note: Gains concentrate in c1/c3/c4. c2, the rare class, LOST 0.011 - full capacity helps the well-represented classes and does nothing for the scarce one.

B7_full_finetune.first_overfitting_in_the_project: Train loss reached 0.0399 (LoRA: 0.0925) and val peaked at epoch 9 then drifted down (0.7148 -> 0.7105 -> 0.7128 -> 0.7117). Every prior diagnosis in this project pointed at UNDERFITTING (head capacity scan, epoch scan, the 0.041 train/test gap). This run crosses the transition, which changes what is worth trying next: augmentation and regularisation now have something to bite on, whereas they would have been counterproductive while underfitting.

B8_full_finetune_augmented.description: Full fine-tune at top-LR 5e-5, gamma 0.85, plus train-time augmentation, 16 epochs. Superseded by B9.

augmentation.ops: hflip p=0.5, vflip p=0.5, brightness/contrast jitter p=0.5 (alpha in [0.8,1.2], beta in [-20,20])
augmentation.applied_to: train only - evaluation is always clean
augmentation.why_no_rotation_or_scale: Both change the 256x1600 input size and therefore the 16x100 patch grid the head is built around; rotation also needs padding that would invent steel texture at the borders. Flips keep the geometry exact.
augmentation.why_photometric_not_colour: Steel imaging varies in illumination, not hue - the images are effectively greyscale.
augmentation.correctness_checks: Flips verified to apply to image AND mask together against m[:,::-1] and m[::-1]; class-pixel histograms preserved under all four flip combinations; photometric verified to leave the mask untouched; uint8 clipping verified in range. Labels are computed AFTER augmenting so patch-majority assignment matches the flipped mask.
augmentation.separate_rng: Augmentation draws from its own stream so it does not perturb the epoch shuffle order, keeping data ordering identical to the un-augmented baseline.

B8_full_finetune_augmented.gain_vs_unaugmented: +0.0079 over the same LR without augmentation (0.7140 -> 0.7219). Epoch-matched at 12 (both bf16): 0.7204 augmented vs 0.7117 unaugmented, +0.0087 - so the gain is augmentation, not the longer schedule.
B8_full_finetune_augmented.epochs_note: Given 16 epochs rather than 12 because augmentation delays overfitting and the unaugmented baseline turned over at epoch 9; holding epochs fixed would have cut the schedule before the benefit appeared.
B8_full_finetune_augmented.regime_change_confirmed: Augmentation reversed the overfitting that full FT introduced. Train loss at epoch 16 was 0.0755 vs the unaugmented run's 0.0399 at epoch 12, and val plateaued (0.7204 at ep12, 0.7182 at ep16) instead of declining. This validates the prediction made when full FT first overfit: data-side levers had headroom precisely because capacity no longer did.
B8_full_finetune_augmented.class_2: First intervention since LoRA to move c2 - 0.6292 (5e-5 plain) -> 0.6411. Still only level with LoRA's 0.6440, so c2 remains the weakest class and is not fixed.

B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.description: BEST RESULT. Full fine-tune at top-LR 1e-4, gamma 0.85, with the B8 augmentation set, 16 epochs. Combines the two levers that had won independently.
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.levers_interact_superadditively: This was predicted to gain under +0.005 on the grounds that the LR curve was flattening. It gained +0.0106 over B8. The prediction was wrong because the flattening was measured WITHOUT augmentation: 5e-5 -> 1e-4 buys +0.0034 unaugmented but +0.0106 augmented, a 3x larger effect. Mechanistically consistent - a higher LR moves pretrained weights further and so overfits harder, meaning it can only pay off fully once augmentation absorbs that overfitting. LR and augmentation are not independent axes and should not have been swept as if they were.
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.class_2_finally_moved: c2 = 0.6646, the best in the project by a clear margin (previous best: LoRA 0.6440, B8 0.6411). c2 had been flat at 0.61-0.64 across LoRA, three LRs, full FT and augmentation-at-5e-5. It took the COMBINATION to move it. c1 likewise set a new best at 0.6562 (previous 0.6399).
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.not_yet_converged: val was still flat-to-rising at the final epoch (0.7324 at ep10 and again at ep16, no decline) and train loss was still falling slowly (0.0720). Unlike the unaugmented runs this one never turned over, so a longer schedule has headroom.
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.dip_pattern_again: Dipped to 0.6533 at epoch 3 and 0.6759 at epoch 5 before recovering - the fourth run in this project to dip mid-schedule and then reach a new best.
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.checkpoint_is_epoch_10: The saved weights are epoch 10's, not epoch 16's. `best` only updates on a strict improvement and epoch 16 tied at 0.7324, so it was never written. They tie on val, so the test number should be materially the same either way - but only epoch 10 was ever measured.
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.val_test_gap: +0.0221 (val 0.7325 -> test 0.7104). This is 3.7x the historical mean gap of +0.0060 across six earlier configs, and roughly double the previous worst (B4 at +0.0116). The pre-registered projection was 0.7235; the actual is 0.7104, so the projection was too optimistic by 0.013 and the error was almost entirely an underestimate of selection pressure (I budgeted ~0.003 for it).
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.why_the_gap_grew: Selection happened at TWO levels, not one: across ~7 configs (three LRs, augment on/off, LoRA vs full FT) and again across epochs WITHIN the winning run. Both selections used the same 1885-image val split. Per-class the damage lands where val estimates are noisiest: c1 -0.0350 and c2 -0.0365, the two rarest classes, while c3 actually IMPROVED by +0.0057. That pattern is the signature of selection noise on scarce classes rather than of a genuine distribution shift between val and test.
B9_full_finetune_augmented_lr1e4.ranking_survives: B9 is still clearly best on TEST, which is the number that counts: 0.7104 vs LoRA's 0.6979 (+0.0125) and the frozen head's 0.6857 (+0.0247). The gains are real; they are just smaller than val implied.

kaggle_metric.peak_properly_bracketed: Unlike the LR sweep, this peak turns over on both sides (1600 -> 0.9518, 3200 -> 0.9464), so 800 is a real optimum rather than the edge of the tested range.
kaggle_metric.kaggle_gap_is_tiny: val 0.9536 -> test 0.9532, a gap of 0.0004, versus +0.0221 on our mean-Dice metric. The Kaggle metric is 85.9% empty-GT pairs, which are easy and stable, so it is far less sensitive to the val selection noise that cost us 0.022 on mean Dice. The two metrics disagree sharply about how much we overfit val.
kaggle_metric.vs_B4_measurement: 0.9235 (B4, the last time this was measured) -> 0.9532. +0.0297.
kaggle_metric.caveat: The published FPN+SE-ResNeXt50 private-LB 0.90038 is on Kaggle's own held-out test set, not ours. Not head-to-head and must not be reported as beating it.
kaggle_metric.min_area_note: min_area thresholds TOTAL predicted area per (image,class), not connected components. It helped both metrics on test (our mean 0.7104 -> 0.7110) but slightly cost our metric on val (0.7325 -> 0.7313); the effect on mean Dice is near-noise either way. Its real value is on the Kaggle metric, where it removes false positives on empty-GT pairs (99.0% -> 99.3% correct).

test_set_ladder.note: Held-out test, pixel-level fp32, global accumulation. The only numbers not subject to val selection.
test_set_ladder.WARNING: The test split has now been used for TEN measurements. It was used for characterisation, not selection, but any claim of the form 'X is our best model' is now a best-of-ten on test and carries the same winner's curse that cost B9 0.022 on val. The only clean number remains B9's 0.7104: selected on val, measured once. Everything else should be read as 'full fine-tuning lands at 0.71-0.72'.

defect_1_ladder.note: defect_1 Dice on the held-out TEST split, every config measured. Requested directly - not the Kaggle metric.
defect_1_ladder.finding: B9 is best on defect_1 too, but only by +0.0029 over LoRA - by far the thinnest margin of any class. Test deltas B6 -> B9: c1 +0.0029, c2 +0.0107, c3 +0.0207, c4 +0.0153. The recent gains came from c3/c4/c2, essentially not from c1.
defect_1_ladder.role_reversal: defect_1 is now the WEAKEST class on test at 0.6212, below defect_2's 0.6281. Class 2 was the problem child for most of this project; the LR+augmentation combination moved it and left class 1 as the floor.

full_test_comparison.note: Every config re-evaluated through ONE code path (live backbone for all three families) so no config gets a different pipeline. Per-class Dice are UNFILTERED. Cross-checked: B4 val reproduces 0.6721 and B4 test reproduces 0.6605, both matching the cached pipeline exactly.
full_test_comparison.headline: B10 (32-epoch single anneal, 1e-4, no augmentation) is nominally best on test at 0.7217, ahead of B7_1e-4's 0.7179. But the top five now span 0.7104-0.7217 (0.0113) and run-to-run variance has never been measured, so this is not a resolvable ranking.
full_test_comparison.caveat: The top four span 0.7104-0.7179, about 0.0075. With 1886 test images that is close to measurement noise, so these are better read as roughly tied than as a clean ranking. What is NOT within noise is that the val ordering failed to predict the test ordering at all.

augmentation_benefit_was_a_val_artifact.conclusion: The 'LR and augmentation stack superadditively' finding does NOT replicate on test. On val the augmented runs gained +0.0079 and +0.0151; on test they gained +0.0022 and LOST 0.0075. Augmentation produced no reliable improvement in generalisation.
augmentation_benefit_was_a_val_artifact.mechanism: val->test gap tracks SELECTION INTENSITY, not augmentation. The unaugmented full-FT runs, which were never the overall winner, have gaps of -0.0017/+0.0001/-0.0005 - essentially zero. The augmented runs have +0.0058 and +0.0221. B9 was both the best-of-configs on val AND a best-of-16-epochs pick (vs best-of-12 for the B7 runs), so its val figure carries the most winner's-curse inflation of anything measured.

min_area_verdict.effect_on_kaggle_metric: Helps everywhere, but the gain shrinks as the model improves: B4 +0.0155, B5 +0.0112, B6 +0.0031, B7_1e-4 +0.0039, B7_5e-5 +0.0025, B9 +0.0022, B8 +0.0012.
min_area_verdict.verdict: It is a metric-specific patch, not a model improvement. It buys score only on the Kaggle metric, where 85.9% of pairs are empty-GT and one stray pixel turns a 1.0 into a 0.0, and it COSTS real segmentation quality on mean Dice by deleting small true positives - which fall disproportionately in c1/c2, the two weakest classes. Its value shrinking monotonically as models improve confirms it compensates for model deficiency. Excluded from headline results.

B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.description: Full FT, top-LR 1e-4, gamma 0.85, NO augmentation, 32 epochs (T_max=32). The one schedule never tested: at epoch 12 a T=32 cosine is still at 69% of peak LR where the 12-epoch runs had annealed to zero.

THE_SAVED_CHECKPOINT_IS_A_SPIKE.neighbourhood_ep14_19: mean 0.7229, std 0.0013 -> ep20 is +0.0060, a 4.6 sigma outlier
THE_SAVED_CHECKPOINT_IS_A_SPIKE.settled_tail_ep21_32: mean 0.7222, std 0.0005 -> ep20 is +0.0067, a 12.5 sigma outlier
THE_SAVED_CHECKPOINT_IS_A_SPIKE.reading: Epoch 20 is almost certainly a lucky epoch on val, not a real improvement. This run's honest val level is ~0.7225. Best-epoch-on-val selection captured a 4.6 sigma fluctuation - a concrete instance of the within-run selection inflation that was underestimated when projecting B9's test score.
THE_SAVED_CHECKPOINT_IS_A_SPIKE.falsifiable_prediction: If the spike is val-specific noise it will NOT transfer: the ep20 checkpoint should score near 0.7220 on test, not 0.7283. Unaugmented full-FT runs have had val->test gaps of ~0.000, so a test score at the settled level rather than the saved level would confirm the spike.

B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.what_32_epochs_actually_bought: Apparent gain over the 12-epoch run at the same LR: 0.7174 -> 0.7283 (+0.0109). Honest gain after discounting the spike: 0.7174 -> ~0.7225 (+0.005). And it cost 20 extra epochs and drove train loss from 0.0500 at ep12 to 0.0067 at ep32 - a 7.5x increase in how hard the model fits its training data for about +0.005 of val.
B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.clearest_overfitting_evidence_in_the_pro: Unlike every earlier ambiguous case, this one is unmistakable: val peaks at ep20 then sits at 0.7222 +/- 0.0005 for twelve straight epochs while train loss falls 2.7x further (0.0181 -> 0.0067). Peak-to-final is 0.0070 against a tail jitter of 0.0005 - 14x. Earlier 'turnover' claims in this project rested on drops of ~0.003 against jitter of ~0.003 and were not supportable; this one is.
B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.tail_is_flat_because_LR_is_zero: The ep21-32 std of 0.0005 is not stability of the model, it is the cosine having annealed to ~0. The model has effectively stopped moving, which is also why no further gain is possible within this schedule.
B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.peak_location: ep20/32 = 0.625 of the schedule, matching B9's 10/16 = 0.625. Peak location continues to track schedule length rather than anything about the data.
B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.PREDICTION_CONFIRMED: Predicted before measuring: if epoch 20 was a val-specific spike, test would land near 0.7220 (the settled level) rather than 0.7283 (the saved val). Actual test: 0.7217 - within 0.0003 of the prediction and 0.0066 below the saved val. Best-epoch-on-val selection inflated that checkpoint by ~0.006. Measured against the settled level the val->test gap is +0.0005, matching the other unaugmented runs.
B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.gain_over_12_epochs: Test 0.7179 (12 ep) -> 0.7217 (32 ep) = +0.0038. So 20 extra epochs and a 7.5x drop in train loss bought under 0.004 on test, which is inside the spread of configs we already cannot separate. The longer single anneal is real but marginal.
B10_full_finetune_32ep_single_anneal.class_2_best_in_project: c2 = 0.6705, the highest anywhere in this project (previous best: B7_1e-4 at 0.6596). c1 also improved to 0.6235 from 0.6090. c4 slipped to 0.7998 from 0.8096.

seed_variance.description: Three runs of an IDENTICAL config (top-LR 1e-4, gamma 0.85, 12 epochs, no augmentation), differing only in shuffle seed. Full FT has no random init at all - the head loads from a checkpoint and the backbone from pretrained weights - so this measures data-ordering variance, which is a LOWER BOUND on true run-to-run spread.
seed_variance.val_sd_is_2.5x_test_sd: Val sd 0.0043 vs test sd 0.0017. Val is the best-of-12-epochs SELECTED number; test is measured at whatever checkpoint val chose, with no further selection. This directly quantifies best-epoch selection inflation and is consistent with the epoch-20 spike in B10 (4.6 sigma) and with B9's +0.0221 gap.

per_class_test_sd.note: The rare classes are the noisy ones. A c1 claim needs ~0.019 and a c2 claim ~0.012 to clear 2 sigma. Most per-class claims made in this project were inside that band.

seed_variance.note_on_stopping: Best-val epoch selection cannot be used to decide schedule length either: the extension's best val epoch was 10 of 16 and its val barely moved (+0.0009), while the quantity that matters moved in the wrong direction by 0.8 points of over-prediction.

significance_verdicts.basis: Compared against the 3-seed mean 0.7199 (se 0.0010); a single-measurement config carries sd 0.0017, so the difference has se 0.0020.

Boundary quality is not false-positive suppression, so it does not get the target-distribution amplification that thresholding, TTA, blackout and the ensemble all got. Useful rule: the amplification applies to interventions that change WHICH pairs fire, not to ones that refine the shape of masks that were already firing.

I predicted the 3rd member would amplify similarly; it delivered 0.24x its holdout estimate instead. Ensemble returns diminish sharply - the amplification rule applies to the FIRST false-positive-suppressing intervention, not to further doses of the same one.

augmentation_verdict_REVERSED.what_was_recorded: 'Augmentation HURT at 1e-4: B9 is 0.0095 below the unaugmented seed mean, 4.7 sigma, SIGNIFICANT.' That was computed correctly and is still true ON OUR SPLIT.
augmentation_verdict_REVERSED.what_the_hidden_test_says: B9 beats B7 by +0.0149 private (0.87237 vs 0.85750) and +0.0062 public.
augmentation_verdict_REVERSED.why_both_are_true: Our test split was carved from train_images, so it shares the training distribution. Augmentation buys robustness to DISTRIBUTION SHIFT, and an in-distribution split is structurally incapable of measuring that - it can only see the cost (a harder training task, slightly worse in-distribution fit) and never the benefit. The 4.7 sigma was real and the conclusion drawn from it was still wrong for the purpose it was used for.
augmentation_verdict_REVERSED.the_general_lesson: Statistical significance is not external validity. A result can be strongly significant on the split you measured and have the opposite sign on the distribution you care about. No amount of seed replication on the wrong distribution would have caught this - only a held-out sample from the target distribution did.
augmentation_verdict_REVERSED.what_this_invalidates: Every ranking in this project was decided on the local split, including the LR sweep, the 32-epoch comparison and the seed analysis. Any of those rankings that hinged on robustness rather than raw fit should now be treated as unverified on the target distribution.
augmentation_verdict_REVERSED.immediate_implication: Augmentation was MILD (hflip, vflip, brightness/contrast alpha 0.8-1.2 beta +/-20). Since even that inverted the ranking, stronger augmentation is now well-motivated rather than speculative.

C1_strong_augmentation.recipe: hflip/vflip p=.5; brightness-contrast p=.5 alpha[0.7,1.3] beta+/-35; gamma p=.3 [0.7,1.4]; gaussian noise p=.3 sigma[3,15]; blur p=.2 sigma[0.3,1.0]; grid distortion p=.3 (+/-8% cell, size-preserving). Weighted toward APPEARANCE because the Kaggle evidence showed over-prediction, not mislocalisation.
C1_strong_augmentation.KEY_FINDING: Extending 16 -> 32 epochs improved LOCAL test by +0.0127 (0.7213 -> 0.7340, the highest local score in the project) while making the TARGET over-prediction rate WORSE (15.7% -> 16.5%). Train loss fell 0.0902 -> 0.0667. More training re-fits the training distribution and undoes the regularisation that augmentation bought - so the extension improved the metric that is anti-correlated with the score we want.
C1_strong_augmentation.c1_calibration: At 16 epochs strong augmentation essentially calibrated c1: 7.4% predicted vs 7.2% true, against B9's 10.2%. Extending pushed it back out to 8.3%. Same direction for c2 (2.9% -> 4.0%, true 2.0%).
C1_strong_augmentation.screen_verdict: The label-free screen says submit the 16-EPOCH model, not the extended one. This is the first time in the project a decision was made on target-distribution evidence before spending a measurement.

label_free_proxy_VALIDATED.out_of_sample_accuracy: Two predictions made BEFORE submitting, from a fit on the first three models: strong@16 predicted 0.8766 / actual 0.87569; strong@32 predicted 0.8710 / actual 0.86978. Both within 0.0012.
label_free_proxy_VALIDATED.why_this_matters: The predicted-positive rate on the competition test images needs NO labels and takes ~5 min locally. It now predicts hidden-test score to about +/-0.001, which means candidates can be screened offline instead of by submission. It is also the only model-selection signal in this project that is not anti-correlated with the target.
label_free_proxy_VALIDATED.CEILING: Extrapolating to 0.90 private demands a 12.1% rate, which is BELOW the true 14.1%. At a perfectly calibrated count the fit gives only 0.8867. So volume reduction alone cannot reach 0.90 - what is needed is suppressing the RIGHT pairs, which is precisely what a presence classifier does and what neither augmentation nor min_area can.
label_free_proxy_VALIDATED.BLIND_SPOT_FOUND: The 12k model scores 0.87625 at a 15.9% rate while strong16 scores 0.87569 at 15.7% - a HIGHER rate with a HIGHER score, breaking monotonicity. The proxy predicted 0.8746, missing by +0.00165 (~3.6 sigma against its prior residual). Cause: predicted-positive rate is a single scalar, but a model can move BOTH error axes at once. Holdout decomposition showed 12k trades +4 false positives for -2 misses and +2 hits versus strong16. The proxy reads only the volume increase and cannot see that part of it is recovered true positives. It remains reliable for models differing mainly in over-prediction (the B7->strong32 family) and is NOT reliable for models differing in training data or anything that shifts misses and false positives in opposite directions.

data_retrain_verdict: Training on 12,068 images instead of 8,797 gave +0.00056 private (0.87569 -> 0.87625). Small but POSITIVE, contradicting the earlier reading of the target rate as a regression. The rate went UP (15.7 -> 15.9) while the score also went up, because the extra predictions included recovered misses. More in-distribution data helps slightly; it was the interpretation of the proxy that was wrong, not the data.

C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.what: iBOT/data2vec-style masked feature prediction on 18,074 unlabelled images (12,568 Severstal-train + 5,506 competition test), 30 epochs, block-wise 60% masking, EMA teacher, backbone 5e-5 with LLRD 0.85.
C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.training_looked_healthy: loss 0.0745 -> 0.0278, cos(pred,target) 0.9194 -> 0.9712, still improving at the end. The SSL objective itself trained fine - that is exactly why the downstream gate mattered.

gate_matched_frozen_probes.note: 8 epochs each, frozen backbone, randomly initialised head, identical everything else.

C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.drift_check: Putting strong16's trained head on each backbone: own backbone 0.7053, STOCK 0.1949, MIM ep10 0.0676, MIM ep30 0.0629. MIM features are LESS compatible with a defect head than untrained stock features - the first sign, before the probes confirmed it.
C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.verdict: Catastrophic forgetting, not domain adaptation. 30 epochs at 5e-5 over 18k images moved the representation away from anything useful for segmentation. Stage 3 (full fine-tune on the MIM backbone) was cancelled on this evidence.
C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.prior_was_already_lukewarm: DINOCell (arXiv 2604.10609) did the same thing with 130k images and found continued pretraining washed out almost entirely under downstream fine-tuning, with gains only in the zero-shot/OOD setting. At 18k images and 7x fewer distinct images per epoch, we got worse than null.
C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.what_would_be_needed_to_retry: Far gentler adaptation - 1e-5 or lower, single-digit epochs - and a frozen probe checked every few epochs rather than only at the end. Not attempted: the top-8 Kaggle solutions all reached 0.90+ with ImageNet-pretrained encoders and no domain pretraining at all, so the evidence that this axis matters here is weak.
C2_masked_pretraining_FAILED.cost: ~9 hours (30 epochs MIM + 2 matched probes), stopped by the gate instead of the planned 14.

D1_triple_thresholding.what: Replaced bare argmax with per-class pixel thresholds [0.60,0.55,0.60,0.60] and min-area [600,1400,1400,3000]. Post-processing only - no retraining. The decision stage every top-8 Severstal solution had and we entirely lacked.
D1_triple_thresholding.tuning: Swept per class against the REAL Kaggle metric on labelled val (strong16, 1885 images). Label thresholds were dropped: redundant with min-area, and the one parameter that HURT out of sample.
D1_triple_thresholding.why_labelled_data_understated_it_7x: In-distribution we make ~56 false positives across 6475 empty pairs (0.9%). On the target we make ~1700 (9.2%). A false-positive remedy measured on data with almost no false positives is measuring almost nothing. Same structure as TTA, which looked worthless on val (+0.0000 rate) and cut the target rate by 0.4 points.
D1_triple_thresholding.proxy_caveat_was_WRONG: I argued the rate->score fit could not score suppression-based interventions because a scalar cannot separate fewer-FPs from fewer-TPs. At 13.0% the fit predicted 0.8942; actual 0.89542, off by 0.0012 and inside its residual band. It holds when suppression is well TARGETED. It failed for presence-gating because that removed more true detections than false ones - the distinction is whether the intervention is selective, not whether it reduces volume.

decision_rule_was_the_biggest_lever: Bare argmax at 15.9% predicted-positive scored 0.87625. Per-class thresholding (13.0%) gave +0.01917, tightening to 11.6% gave +0.00267, and 3-view TTA gave +0.00085. Total +0.02269 private from POST-PROCESSING ALONE, no retraining. For comparison the entire modelling arc - LoRA, full fine-tuning, strong augmentation, 37% more data - moved private by about the same amount and cost roughly 40 GPU-hours.

D2_lovasz_FAILED_TO_TRANSFER.what: 8-epoch Lovasz-softmax phase at 2e-5 resumed from 12k_ep16, matching the two-phase recipe 5th and 9th place describe (pixel loss first, then Lovasz at reduced LR).

in_distribution_it_WON.holdout_dice: 0.7130 -> 0.7371 (+0.0241, biggest model gain of the project)

D2_lovasz_FAILED_TO_TRANSFER.undertrained_caveat: Best epoch was 8 of 8, still improving - so this is a lower bound on Lovasz. But the in-distribution/target sign flip is what matters, and more epochs would likely widen it rather than close it.
D2_lovasz_FAILED_TO_TRANSFER.threshold_note: Lovasz needed completely different thresholds (pixel 0.60/0.20/0.20/0.30 vs 0.60/0.55/0.60/0.60) because optimising IoU pushes probabilities toward confident 0/1. Its holdout-tuned thresholds put it at 15.9% on target, so the submitted set was rate-matched to 11.05% instead.
D2_lovasz_FAILED_TO_TRANSFER.the_pattern: Every FITTING improvement in this project failed to transfer: capacity, LoRA rank, epochs, more data (+0.0006), MIM (negative), Lovasz (negative). Every ROBUSTNESS or DECISION-RULE improvement did: augmentation (+0.015, and it LOWERED in-distribution score), thresholding (+0.022), TTA (+0.001). In-distribution metrics on this problem are close to useless for predicting target performance, and were sometimes anti-correlated.

extended_to_13_epochs.verdict: Training Lovasz to convergence made it WORSE on target, not better. The undertraining objection was fair and is now answered: holdout 0.7130/0.7371/0.7422 maps to target 0.89894/0.89084/0.88789 - a perfect inverse ordering within one model family, with training length as the only variable.

THE_CENTRAL_FINDING.claim: On this problem, in-distribution segmentation quality is ANTI-correlated with hidden-test score, and the two categories of intervention behave in opposite directions.

robustness_and_decision_improvements_tha.strong augmentation: LOWERED local Dice, target +0.0034 (and mild aug over none was +0.015)

THE_CENTRAL_FINDING.practical_rule: Any intervention that makes the model fit Severstal-train better should be assumed not to transfer until a submission says otherwise. Any intervention that constrains the model or changes the decision rule is worth testing. Local Dice was actively misleading as a selection signal - Spearman -1.00 across the augmentation family, and perfectly inverse across the Lovasz training-length family.
THE_CENTRAL_FINDING.HOLDOUT_IS_INVERTED_FOR_MODEL_SELECTION: Confirmed three times: ViT-B (holdout last -> best backbone), LoRA (holdout 0.94239 vs blackout 0.95093 -> tied on target), BCE (holdout below blackout -> beats it). Rank models by SUBMITTING them. The holdout remains sound for decision-rule tuning (thresholds, TTA, bilinear, the c3 min_area direction all held up).

E1_postprocessing_sweep_2026-08-31.what: Three never-deployed decision-rule changes, swept offline against the real Kaggle metric on cached probabilities. No GPU.

bilinear_upsampling.verdict: KEEP. We expand stride-4 probabilities with np.repeat (nearest neighbour), so every boundary is a 4px staircase. Interpolating the probability map and thresholding at full res costs one line.

morphological_cleanup.bug_found: First implementation scored -0.039 because the hole fill seeded floodFill at (0,0); when a defect touches that corner the flood fills the DEFECT and every background pixel then reads as an interior hole. c3 blobs are large and often touch borders. Fixed by padding with a guaranteed-background border.

E2_sigmoid_bce_2026-08-31.rationale: The Kaggle metric scores each (ImageId, ClassId) pair independently, so a softmax forcing classes to compete for probability mass does not match how the score is computed.
E2_sigmoid_bce_2026-08-31.verdict: SUPERSEDED - see verdict_corrected. The 'FAILS' call was holdout-based and wrong.
E2_sigmoid_bce_2026-08-31.measurement_error_caught: First scored WITH 3-view TTA against blackout's no-TTA cache, which made BCE look +0.0003 better. Re-cached matched and the sign flipped negative.
E2_sigmoid_bce_2026-08-31.REVISED_CATEGORISATION: The old 'robustness 5/5 vs fitting 0/7' split needs correcting. The real line is whether the model is RETRAINED. Post-hoc decision changes - thresholds, TTA, ensembling, bilinear upsampling - are 6 for 6. Retraining interventions - capacity, 32 epochs, +37% data, MIM, Lovasz x2, sigmoid/BCE - are 1 for 7, the single success being blackout augmentation. This predicts a ViT-B fine-tune is unlikely to pay.
E2_sigmoid_bce_2026-08-31.verdict_corrected: bce16 scored 0.90082 on target, beating blackout (0.89933, identical recipe bar the loss) by +0.00149 and every other single model. The holdout ranked it BELOW blackout (0.95221 vs 0.95324) and I called it a failure on that basis, including as an ensemble partner. Third inversion in a row after ViT-B and LoRA. The metric scores each (ImageId, ClassId) pair independently, so a per-class sigmoid matches the objective's structure while a softmax forces classes to compete for mass they never compete for.

fp16_vs_fp32.verdict: IDENTICAL. fp16 rounding on softmax outputs is ~1e-3 against decision margins of ~0.05, so it cannot flip pair decisions. Use fp16 always.
fp16_vs_fp32.consequence: Halving inference cost re-opens the 3-member ensemble: 9 fp16 passes ~50 min, inside the 1hr kernel limit. Previously ruled out on fp32 timings.

rate_curve_turned.note: First reversal after monotonic gains from 15.9% down. The optimum is at or above 10.97%, so the direction to explore is looser, not tighter. E4_vitb_full_finetune_2026-09-01.calibration_finding: The sweep wants pix 0.70 on ALL FOUR classes for ViT-B vs 0.60/0.45 for ViT-S - uniform across classes, so it is real signal: ViT-B is systematically more confident and ViT-S-tuned thresholds make it over-fire. E4_vitb_full_finetune_2026-09-01.verdict_corrected: ViT-B alone scored 0.90006 on the target, beating blackout's 0.89933 and every other single model. The holdout ranked it LAST at fixed thresholds (0.95035 vs blackout 0.95093) and I concluded against it. That was the eighth time in this project that in-distribution ranking inverted on the hidden set, and I still treated the holdout as decisive. The user overrode the recommendation on exactly that reasoning.
E4_vitb_full_finetune_2026-09-01.METHODOLOGICAL_LESSON: For MODEL SELECTION the holdout is not merely noisy, it is inverted, and no amount of care about matched thresholds or noise floors fixes a sign error. It remains sound for DECISION-RULE tuning, where thresholds/TTA/ensembling predictions have held up. Rank models on the target rate or by spending a submission; use the holdout only to choose post-processing.

E5_backbone_scaling_probe_2026-09-01.what: Frozen-backbone probes, 6 epochs, cold randomly-initialised head, identical settings. Only the backbone varies, so this isolates pretrained feature quality from fitting capacity.
E5_backbone_scaling_probe_2026-09-01.scaling: S->B +0.0198, B->L +0.0110. Bigger keeps helping, with returns roughly halving per step against 3.5x the parameters.
E5_backbone_scaling_probe_2026-09-01.measured_cost_per_epoch: ViT-S 442s, ViT-B 634s (1.54x), ViT-L 1275s (2.88x). My FLOPs extrapolations said 4x for ViT-B (wrong by 2.6x) and 3.5x for ViT-L (close). Both were guesses where a measurement was cheap.
E5_backbone_scaling_probe_2026-09-01.DEPLOYMENT_VERDICT: ViT-L is the best backbone and still probably not worth using. ViT-B's +0.0198 frozen became +0.00073 on target as a single model; scaling that, ViT-L implies ~+0.0004 over ViT-B solo, landing near 0.9005. But ViT-L 3-view inference is ~52 min of the 60 min Kaggle budget, leaving no room for an ensemble partner - and cross-architecture ensembling is worth +0.00276. Net negative by ~0.002 versus the current 0.90335 ensemble.
E5_backbone_scaling_probe_2026-09-01.hardware_note: ViT-L full FT on the 8GB card is ~40 hr (300M params + AdamW = 4.8GB before activations forces bs=2). On a 48GB card ~8-12 hr. The Kaggle 1 hr INFERENCE limit is unaffected by training hardware, so the ensembling trade-off stands either way.
E5_backbone_scaling_probe_2026-09-01.code_changes: train_full_ft.py now derives N_BLOCKS/MAX_DEPTH from the loaded config and rescales taps proportionally ((2,5,8,11) -> (5,11,17,23) for 24 blocks). The hardcoded MAX_DEPTH=13 would have given deep ViT-L blocks gamma**-12 = ~142x the base LR - a silent divergence that would have looked like 'ViT-L does not train'.

E6_lora_coverage_vs_rank_2026-09-02.what: ViT-L, LoRA, blackout aug, 1500 train images, 3 epochs, holdout eval, seed 0. Varies which Linear modules get adapters, and rank.
E6_lora_coverage_vs_rank_2026-09-02.finding: Coverage +0.0282; doubling rank +0.0009. all6_r8 (3.54M) beats qkv_r16 (2.36M) by +0.0273 on only 1.5x the parameters - it is WHERE the capacity goes, not how much.
E6_lora_coverage_vs_rank_2026-09-02.why_the_old_rank_sweep_was_flat: train_lora.py only ever targeted q_proj/k_proj/v_proj - 3 of 6 Linears per block, ~25% of block weights, never touching the MLP (up_proj/down_proj) which holds two thirds of the parameters. Rank could not reach past that ceiling, which is why r4->r16 was flat while full FT beat LoRA by 0.0220 at 11 sigma. results.json already flagged that conclusion as SUPERSEDED; I quoted it as settled anyway.
E6_lora_coverage_vs_rank_2026-09-02.design_flaw_in_this_sweep: alpha was left at 16 for both ranks, so effective scale alpha/r was 1.0 at r16 and 2.0 at r8 - rank and update magnitude are confounded. The historical sweep held alpha=2r for exactly this reason. The COVERAGE comparison is unaffected (r and alpha both fixed, only targets varied). The rank comparison is one-directional: r8 tied r16 despite 2x the effective scale, so rank saturating is the safe reading.
E6_lora_coverage_vs_rank_2026-09-02.caveat: 3 epochs on 1500 images measures EARLY training and biases against high capacity - all6_r16 started at 0.1687 vs qkv's 0.3358 and overtook by epoch 3, still gaining +0.132/epoch vs qkv's +0.077. The gap would likely widen with more data and epochs.
E6_lora_coverage_vs_rank_2026-09-02.decision: Use all-6 coverage at r=16, alpha=16 - the exact configuration measured. Epoch times held flat (673/685/695s) with no memory-pressure decay.

E8_what_drives_ensemble_gain_2026-09-04.method: For each of 8 candidate 5th members: disagreement with the 4-member base on the empty/non-empty decision (the call the Kaggle metric scores), against the measured holdout ensemble gain from adding it.

result.disagreement_range: 0.70%-1.00% across all 8 - they are all similarly diverse, so diversity cannot be what separates +0.00108 from -0.00121

E8_what_drives_ensemble_gain_2026-09-04.VERDICT: MEMBER QUALITY drives ensemble gain; DIVERSITY does not. The 'equal quality' rule stated early in the project was correct. The 'cross-architecture diversity is why it works' story added later was a rationalisation - it was used to justify keeping lora_r8, to rank vitl_bce over vitb_lora, and to argue for ConvNeXt.
E8_what_drives_ensemble_gain_2026-09-04.lora_r8_re_explained: It helped (+0.00194 on target) because on the TARGET it is equal quality (0.89961 vs vitb 0.90006, bce16 0.90082, blackout 0.89933). Only the holdout ranked it last (0.94239). That is the inversion, not diversity.
E8_what_drives_ensemble_gain_2026-09-04.uncomfortable_consequence: Gain is driven by quality, but holdout quality has been inverted against target quality five times. The holdout gives the RELATIONSHIP (quality -> gain) while being unable to supply the INPUT (which model is good). Member selection therefore requires submitting. Any candidate ranking based on holdout solo scores - including the lovasz > vitl_lora > strong16 ordering - is weak evidence.
E8_what_drives_ensemble_gain_2026-09-04.caveats: 8 candidates, gains measured on 500 images where +0.0005 is one pair, and disagreement was measured only on the empty/non-empty call - mask-shape diversity is not captured.

E10_rank_curve_and_lora_vs_fullft_2026-0.FULL_FT_BUYS_NOTHING: 331k adapters match 21.6M fully fine-tuned parameters: +0.0008 snapshot, +0.0042 best, both favouring LoRA. This supersedes the historical 'full FT beats LoRA by 0.0220 at 11 sigma', which used q/k/v-only adapters - coverage was the binding constraint, not capacity.
E10_rank_curve_and_lora_vs_fullft_2026-0.HEAD_DOMINATES: The segmentation head is 11,094,096 params. Across the whole sweep total trainable moves only 11.4M -> 13.8M while rank varies 8x. 'Rank saturates' may be better stated as 'the head dominates trainable capacity, so rank barely moves the total'.
E10_rank_curve_and_lora_vs_fullft_2026-0.INTERPRETATION_PENDING: Every difference in this table is <=0.0047. Seed variance on this exact recipe is being measured now; if it comes back near +/-0.003 then none of these differences are distinguishable and the table says only 'rank, and full FT vs LoRA, do not matter'.

E11_seed_variance_2026-09-05.design: Identical to vits_ft10 - ViT-S, 12k, blackout, warm head, 10-epoch cosine, holdout - differing ONLY in shuffle seed. Full FT has no random init (head loads from checkpoint, backbone from pretrained), so this is data-ordering variance, a LOWER BOUND on true run-to-run spread.
E11_seed_variance_2026-09-05.n2_estimate_was_wrong: The two-seed figure was 0.0035 and understated sigma by 2.5x. Two points cannot estimate a spread; seed 2 landed 0.0168 above seed 0.

RESCORED_AGAINST_SIGMA_0.0089.lora_coverage_qkv_to_all6: +0.0282 = 3.2 sigma - SURVIVES, the only local finding in the project that clears the noise floor

E11_seed_variance_2026-09-05.caveat_frozen_probes: The backbone comparisons were frozen probes (head-only training), plausibly a lower-variance regime than full fine-tuning. Applying this sigma to them is conservative, but frozen-probe seed variance was never measured.
E11_seed_variance_2026-09-05.caveat_lora_runs: This sigma is for ViT-S FULL fine-tuning. The rank curve was LoRA; its seed variance is unmeasured and assumed similar.
E11_seed_variance_2026-09-05.STRUCTURAL_LESSON: A 500-image holdout with single-seed runs cannot resolve the 0.001-0.01 effects this project spent weeks chasing. One (image,class) pair is 0.0005 of the Kaggle metric there. Multiple seeds per config were needed from the start - 3x the cost per experiment, and it would have prevented a long series of confident conclusions drawn from noise.
E11_seed_variance_2026-09-05.copypaste_bar: Needs to beat the 3-seed mean of 0.69377 by ~0.018 (2 sigma) to register. Treat the result as uninformative unless dramatic.

E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.what: 8 single models with BOTH a holdout score (bilinear, at submitted thresholds) and a Kaggle private score. The definitive test of the project's central claim.
E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.rank_changes: holdout #1 blackout -> target #5; holdout #8 lora_r8 -> target #3; holdout #6 bce16 -> target #1; holdout #4 lovasz -> target #8
E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.CORRECTION_TO_EARLIER_FRAMING: This project repeatedly described the holdout as 'INVERTED'. That is wrong and it flatters the holdout. An inverted validation set shows a strongly NEGATIVE correlation and remains useful - you flip it. What we have is r = -0.12, p = 0.65: NO CORRELATION. The ranking is scrambled, not reversed. The earlier 'five documented inversions' were individual cases sampled from a relationship that is simply noise.
E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.consequence: For MODEL SELECTION the holdout carries no information and never did. It remained useful for DECISION-RULE tuning (thresholds, TTA, bilinear, the c3 min_area direction) - those are measured on the same fixed model, where the split's job is different.
E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.epochs_10_vs_16_ANSWERED: vits_ft10 0.89960 vs blackout (16ep) 0.89933 = +0.00027. Tied. Holdout claimed 16 was better by +0.0067; that did not transfer. The 10-epoch candidate models were never handicapped.
E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.lora_beats_full_FT_ON_TARGET: vits_lora_r16 0.90063 vs vits_ft10 0.89960 = +0.00103, matched schedule/data/head-init/seed. 1.33M adapters beat 21.6M fully fine-tuned parameters on the hidden set, not just locally.
E12_THE_HOLDOUT_IS_UNCORRELATED_2026-09-.taps_matter_ON_TARGET: vits_taps 0.89539 vs vits_ft10 0.89960 = -0.00421, the largest single-model effect measured. The holdout scored this difference at +0.0032 and the seed study called it noise - on target it is real and in the same direction.

E13_copy_paste_2026-09-05.what: strong + defect_blackout + COPY-PASTE vs strong + defect_blackout (vits_ft10). One variable. Pastes a donor defect's ACTUAL MASK SHAPE (not its bbox) from another image in the same batch, with brightness matched on the BACKGROUND inside the bbox so the defect's contrast against its surroundings survives.
E13_copy_paste_2026-09-05.verdict: NO BENEFIT. Below the 3-seed mean, inside the noise band. Needed +0.018 (2 sigma) to register as positive; came in at -0.010.
E13_copy_paste_2026-09-05.honest_limit: This setup cannot resolve +/-0.018, so the correct statement is 'no benefit shown and a small one could not have been detected' - not 'copy-paste does not work'. Consistent with the original argument for deprioritising it (we over-predict on target, so adding positives pushes the wrong way) but not a demonstration of it.
E13_copy_paste_2026-09-05.implementation_bug_caught: First version matched brightness on the DEFECT pixels, which shifts them to the destination's background level and makes every pasted defect invisible - it would have trained on positive labels over untouched steel and looked like 'copy-paste hurts'. Caught by a synthetic test before the run.

E14_WARM_HEAD_LP_FT_2026-09-06.finding: Head initialisation is worth +0.0535 on holdout - 6 sigma against the measured seed floor of 0.0089, and the second-largest effect in the project after LoRA coverage (+0.0282).

comparison.matched_on: LoRA r16 alpha32 all-6, train12k, blackout aug, 10 epochs, seed 0, same backbone, same decoder. Only --init-head differs.

E14_WARM_HEAD_LP_FT_2026-09-06.what_the_warm_head_is: spatial_conv_up4_h1024_wp0.3_dice1.0_ep30.pt - an 11M conv head trained 30 epochs on FROZEN DINOv3 features in the early spatial-head phase. This is LP-FT: starting fine-tuning from a trained probe so random-head gradients do not distort pretrained backbone features. LP-FT was proposed specifically to improve OOD performance, which is this project's failure mode.
E14_WARM_HEAD_LP_FT_2026-09-06.CONFOUND_IN_EVERY_BACKBONE_COMPARISON: The warm head's first conv is (1024,1536,1,1), sized for ViT-S's 4x384. ViT-B needs 3072 and ViT-L needs 4096, so BOTH always trained COLD while every ViT-S model trained WARM. The backbone comparisons - ViT-B 0.90006 and ViT-L 0.89956 against ViT-S 0.90063 on target - were warm-ViT-S versus cold-ViT-B/L, with a 6 sigma handicap on one side. Backbone scale may never have been tested fairly.
next_tests: Submit joint_conv: the drop from vits_lora_r16's 0.90063 measures whether the warm head's advantage transfers to target.
Train a conv head on FROZEN ViT-B features (~2.5h), then use it as --init-head for a joint ViT-B run - the first fair test a larger backbone would have had.
E14_WARM_HEAD_LP_FT_2026-09-06.caveat: This is a holdout measurement, and the holdout is uncorrelated with target for model selection (E12, r=-0.12). The magnitude is far above noise, but transfer is unverified until joint_conv is submitted.

E15_decoder_architecture_2026-09-06.design: conv (1x1 -> 3x3 -> 1x1, PixelShuffle(4) reaching stride 4 in ONE step) vs progressive (16->8->4 with a 3x3 conv AFTER each x2 upsample). Parameters matched: 11.09M vs 11.19M. Tested under two training regimes.

joint_training.note: LoRA r16 alpha32 all-6, 12k, blackout, 10ep, both cold-headed

E15_decoder_architecture_2026-09-06.verdict: PROGRESSIVE WINS. +0.0391 at 4.4 sigma under joint training - the regime that matters. The single PixelShuffle means every pixel in a 4x4 block comes from one 1x1 projection of one stride-16 feature with no spatial computation afterwards; progressive computes at stride 8 and 4 as well.
E15_decoder_architecture_2026-09-06.why_frozen_understated_it: Under a frozen backbone the decoder can only reshape fixed features. Jointly, the backbone adapts TO the decoder, so a decoder able to use finer detail also changes what the backbone learns to provide. The screening test was directionally right and understated the effect 3x.
E15_decoder_architecture_2026-09-06.frozen_scores_higher_than_joint: conv frozen 0.6802 > conv joint 0.6376 because the frozen runs started from vits_lora_r16's ALREADY FINE-TUNED backbone, while the joint runs started from stock DINOv3. Not comparable across regimes; only within.
E15_decoder_architecture_2026-09-06.still_missing: warm head + progressive. vits_lora_r16 (warm+conv) 0.6911 still beats cold+progressive 0.6767, so the two effects have never been combined.

E16_warm_head_on_vitb_2026-09-06.why: The warm head is ViT-S shaped (1536 in), so every ViT-B and ViT-L model in this project trained COLD while every ViT-S trained WARM - a confound in every backbone comparison. Cold cost -0.00627 on TARGET for ViT-S (vits_lora_r16 0.90063 vs jnt_conv 0.89436), the only local finding that transferred.
E16_warm_head_on_vitb_2026-09-06.method: Stage 1: conv head on FROZEN ViT-B features, 10 epochs -> 0.6658. Stage 2: joint ViT-B LoRA r16 alpha32 all-6 using it as --init-head. Matched to vitb_lora in every other respect.
E16_warm_head_on_vitb_2026-09-06.INITIALISATION_vs_TOTAL_TRAINING: ViT-S's warm head had 30 epochs of frozen pretraining and gave +0.0535; ViT-B's had 10 and gave +0.0173 - about a third. So the benefit is NOT purely a better starting point; the extra head pretraining does real work. Those two were confounded in the ViT-S warm head, and stage 1 was run at 10 epochs deliberately to separate them. Imperfect - the backbones differ too - but it points at total training carrying a substantial share.
E16_warm_head_on_vitb_2026-09-06.next: A 30-epoch frozen ViT-B head (~7.5h vs 2.5h) would plausibly recover more. And vitb_lora_warm needs submitting: vs vitb_lora's 0.89953 on target.

E17_complementarity_2026-09-07.method: Empty/non-empty decisions for 10 models on all 5,506 COMPETITION TEST images (22,024 image-class decisions) at pixel[.60,.60,.60,.45] min_area[1050,2450,1750,5250]. Label-free, so measurable on the target distribution itself - unlike E8, which used the holdout and correlated against gains inside the noise floor.
E17_complementarity_2026-09-07.finding: The ensemble is NOT diversity-selected. Members span 3.22-4.28% and non-members 3.17-3.87% - overlapping. It contains one of the LEAST diverse models (vits_lora_r16) and excludes the two most diverse non-members. Confirms the user's suspicion that it is 'a mix of the best ones' rather than models chosen to cover each other's errors.
E17_complementarity_2026-09-07.but_diversity_did_not_pay: Adding the most complementary non-member was neutral (-0.00003). Combined with quality-weighting HURTING (-0.00043), the picture is that member choice barely matters at 5 members - the ensemble is saturated.
E17_complementarity_2026-09-07.caveat: Measured at the old threshold set, not the current best [.65,.60,.65,.58]/[630,1470,1050,3150]. Ordering unlikely to change (the top two non-members are 0.5 points clear) but the exact figures are tied to that operating point.

E18_longer_head_phase_2026-09-07.question: Does a longer frozen-head phase produce a better joint model? ViT-S's warm head had 30 epochs and gave +0.00627 on target; ViT-B's had 10 and gave +0.00471, suggesting more helps.
E18_longer_head_phase_2026-09-07.method: Clean 20-epoch frozen ViT-B head from scratch (single cosine, NOT a resume - the 10+10 resume attempt fell 0.6658 -> 0.6431 the moment the LR restarted), then the identical joint LoRA run.
E18_longer_head_phase_2026-09-07.finding: The head got +0.022 BETTER and the joint model got 0.0059 WORSE. Consistent with over-specialisation: a head fitted harder to FROZEN features is a worse starting point once the backbone starts moving. Within noise (0.66 sigma), so 'no improvement' is the safe reading rather than 'worse'.
E18_longer_head_phase_2026-09-07.caveat: Local only. The holdout is uncorrelated with target for model selection (E12, r=-0.12), so this cannot settle the target ordering - a submission can.
E18_longer_head_phase_2026-09-07.verdict_pending_submission: On local evidence, do not extend the head phase. 10 epochs is enough or better.

E20_context_usage_windowed_inference_202.question: Before any crop training: how much do full-strip models use context beyond a 512-px window, and does crop geometry need a position fix?
E20_context_usage_windowed_inference_202.method: src/context_diag.py. vitb_lora_warm and vits_lora_r16 (no test exposure; pseudo student excluded - memorised test predictions). Modes: full strip; 256x512 windows stride 256 stitched by max edge margin (>=130 px context each side); same windows WITHOUT position fix. Position fix = each window gets its slice of the full-strip RoPE grid (DINOv3 normalises patch positions to [-1,1] over the given image, so a bare 512-px window has 3.1x wider spacing). Self-tests: coordinate slice exact, full-width window reproduces plain forward exactly, full-view test decisions reproduce E17 exactly on 64 images.
E20_context_usage_windowed_inference_202.side_finding: DINOv3 config pos_embed_rescale=2.0: in train mode RoPE coords are already randomly rescaled x[0.5,2] during every fine-tune in this project; eval uses exact coords. A 3.1x crop mismatch is outside that range.

holdout.reading: Windows worse in both backbones (Kaggle -0.0081 ViT-B, -0.0050 ViT-S), mostly c3 decisions and c1 Dice; no class gains in decisions. Without the position fix, worse again in both (c2 Dice collapses) - the fix is required for any crop training. Caveat: models never trained on windows, so this is an upper bound on information loss, not the intrinsic value of context.

test_5506.reading: Test is 2-8x more context-sensitive than holdout (c3 2.1-2.5x, c1 3.5-7.8x). Removing context makes c3 fire MORE in both backbones (net +186 ViT-B, +120 ViT-S): full-strip context suppresses c3 on test. c4 is context-insensitive (~0.3%). c1/c2 net direction differs by backbone.

which_images.cross_backbone_overlap: context-flipped images are shared far above chance: c3 window-only 93 in both vs 14.6 expected (6.4x), c3 full-only 8.2x, c1 15-19x - a property of the images, not model noise; but only ~30-37% shared
which_images.ensemble_uncertainty: flips sit in the 0.90756 ensemble's uncertain region: c3 members split 54.7% (window-only) / 66.8% (full-only) vs 11.9% on unflipped images; c1 41.8% / 76.4% vs 3.8%
which_images.ensemble_side: the ensemble sides with the full view: c3 window-only images are ensemble-positive 16.6% (6.5% where both models flip) vs 33.3% elsewhere; full-only 54.6%. CAVEAT: circular - every member is itself a full-strip model sharing the same context use, so this is not independent evidence that full context is right on test.

implications: Position fix mandatory for any crop or windowed use.

Plain crop training discards context both backbones use; on test it would push c3 toward firing on images the Kaggle-validated ensemble rejects, against every c3-suppression result so far. Lower prior than assumed.
If crops at all: DINO direction (crop matches full view), which preserves the context behaviour rather than removing it. No evidence yet of a target-side gain mechanism.
Only direct test of direction: submit windowed inference for vitb_lora_warm vs its full-view 0.90424 (kernel patch, no training).

E23_simplex_etf_head_AB_2026-09-16.question: Does a FIXED simplex-ETF classifier (Yang et al. NeurIPS 2022, arXiv 2203.09081) fine-tune better than our learned 1x1 classifier? Suggested for imbalance and open-set rejection.

what_the_literature_says.fixed_ETF_classifier: rare classes cannot lose classifier norm to frequent ones (imbalance mechanism)
what_the_literature_says.segmentation_evidence: Zhong et al. CVPR 2023 (arXiv 2301.01100) do NOT fix the classifier - they regularise feature centres toward ETF structure, because context and imbalance break it
what_the_literature_says.open_set_claim: not free - published simplex open-set methods add explicit rejection terms; a 5-vertex ETF with background as a vertex still assigns every pixel to a vertex
what_the_literature_says.correction_to_the_suggestion: PixelShuffle is the CAUSE of the 4px staircase, not a cure; and the final layer is 1024->80 (5 classes x 16 sub-pixels), so the simplex version emits 16 x etf_dim channels and normalises per sub-pixel

Unit-tested: exact ETF geometry, gradients to trunk/out/scale only, exact state-dict round-trip, finite under autocast. Kaggle cell patched with a matching SimplexHead - verified bit-identical to the training head on the bundle weights.

verdicts: Conservative edges: right direction, small effect. 1 px erosion +0.00057 holdout (+0.00135 train); 2 px ~0; more hurts. Retraining on eroded GT would bake in roughly this uniform bias - not worth a retrain.
